sources_examined.title: Dual MPC for Active Learning of Nonparametric Uncertainties
sources_examined.mechanism: Gaussian-process posterior covariance is included in MPC so control actions can deliberately visit informative states while retaining regulation and robust constraint satisfaction.
sources_examined.reason: Primary abstract and available preprint metadata establish the dual-effect mechanism and nonlinear/robot demonstrations, but this pass did not extract a clean quantitative improvement over a matched passive-learning controller. Do not promote as a quantified candidate yet.

sources_examined.title: Model predictive control with active learning for stochastic systems with structural model uncertainty: Online model discrimination
sources_examined.mechanism: Augment control cost with predicted Bayes risk of model-selection error so actions both control the process and discriminate among structural model hypotheses.
sources_examined.reason: Matched comparisons against nominal MPC, passive-learning MPC, and robust MPC exist and the paper reports significant advantages in a nonlinear bioreactor, but accessible text in this pass did not provide a compact numeric effect size.

sources_examined.title: Dual Control with Active Learning using Gaussian Process Regression
sources_examined.mechanism: Quantify information acquired by each control action with entropy and jointly optimize identification and control objectives.
sources_examined.reason: Useful conceptual precursor, but the available source summary gives demonstrations rather than a sufficiently strong quantitative comparison.

new_transfer_hypothesis: A research system could choose actions that simultaneously make task progress and maximally reduce uncertainty about which internal mechanism/model is correct, rather than separating exploitation work from diagnostic experiments. This is structurally different from CF-20260825-04: the informative probe is embedded inside the action/control objective rather than scheduled as a separate experiment.
scope_warning: No dual-control result is promoted to the quantified candidate list in this run because the numeric matched-baseline evidence was not yet extracted. Mechanistic plausibility is not treated as demonstrated transfer value.
